options.B: It involves more extensive tissue removal including the labia minora.
options.C: It is performed exclusively in hospital operating theatres.
options.D: It does not involve any form of scarring or healing complications.

explanation: Spot on! Type II builds on Type I by also removing the labia minora.

question: What is a dangerous misconception regarding mental health in older adults?

options.A: Recognizing that memory loss can have multiple causes
options.B: Believing that clinical depression is a normal part of aging
options.C: Understanding that retirement can cause psychological stress
options.D: Knowing that social isolation impacts emotional well-being

explanation: Depression is never a normal part of aging and always requires proper assessment and treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which animal is the primary natural reservoir and transmitter of Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Migratory birds
options.B: Multimammate rats
options.C: Freshwater fish
options.D: Domesticated dogs

explanation: The multimammate rat sheds the Lassa virus in its urine and droppings, which can contaminate human food and living areas. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h3)

question: When stripping a dirty bed, what is the correct way to handle the used linen?

options.A: Roll it inward toward the center to trap dirt and microbes
options.B: Shake each sheet vigorously to remove loose hair
options.C: Toss the bundle across the room into the laundry chute
options.D: Fold each sheet into a square and place on the floor

explanation: You nailed it! Rolling the dirty linen inward traps skin flakes, dust, and germs so they don't fly into the air or onto your clothes.

question: Why are new mums at high risk for their bladders getting overly full right after birth?

options.A: Decreased bladder sensation and birth trauma
options.B: Complete failure of the ureters to drain urine
options.C: High levels of circulating oxytocin in the blood
options.D: A sudden permanent drop in glomerular filtration

explanation: Swelling around the birth area and lingering numbness can trick the bladder, making it hard to empty fully. Good nursing care means keeping a close eye on this!

question: What is the main reason a bag of blood must be completely infused within four hours?

options.A: To ensure the infusion pump battery does not run out of power
options.B: To prevent dangerous bacterial growth in the blood at room temperature
options.C: To stop the patient from becoming too cold during the procedure
options.D: To prevent the red blood cells from settling at the bottom of the bag

explanation: Blood is warm and rich in nutrients—bacteria love it too! Finishing it within four hours stops germs from multiplying in the bag.

question: Under most Nigerian laws, what is the main legal exception that allows for an abortion?

options.A: If the family cannot afford a child
options.B: When requested by the husband
options.C: If the pregnancy occurs during school term
options.D: To save the life of the pregnant woman

explanation: Nigerian law is very strict regarding abortion, but saving the mother's life is recognized as a legal exception. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is building trust so important during a reproductive health check-in?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking questions about treatment costs
options.B: It encourages the patient to share sensitive personal information honestly
options.C: It guarantees the patient will accept all prescribed medications
options.D: It replaces the need for a detailed physical examination

explanation: Great nursing care starts with a good relationship! When patients trust you, they feel safe sharing personal details about their sexual or menstrual health without fear of judgment.

question: Which group of professionals should a nurse collaborate with when supporting a forced marriage survivor?

options.A: Commercial advertising agencies and public relations firms
options.B: Private financial investors and real estate agents
options.C: Only hospital pharmacists and laboratory technicians
options.D: Social workers, legal aid providers, and law enforcement

explanation: A strong support network requires medical, legal, and social protection experts working together to keep the survivor safe. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h7)

question: How can nurses best help prevent FGM within local communities?

options.A: By educating families and working with local leaders to change attitudes
options.B: By reporting every pregnant woman to international human rights courts
options.C: By offering safe, clean clinical alternatives for young girls
options.D: By focusing only on treating women who already have complications

explanation: Prevention relies on grassroots education and community engagement to address the root cultural drivers of FGM. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why should you ask a patient to close their eyes during a sensory touch test?

options.A: To measure if the patient can stay awake under stress
options.B: To prevent visual cues from helping them guess the stimulus
options.C: To help the patient fall asleep during a long examination
options.D: To protect the eyes from bright room lights and glare

explanation: Closing their eyes ensures they rely purely on their nerves and touch, rather than cheating by peeking at what you are doing!

question: Which of the following is NOT required under standard precautions for a routine physical check?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves if contact with body fluids is expected
options.B: Cleaning stethoscope bells and diaphragms between patients
options.C: Performing proper hand hygiene before touching the patient
options.D: Wearing a full sterile surgical gown for a simple pulse check

explanation: Routine physical checks do not require sterile surgical gowns unless you are performing a sterile invasive procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: According to the Nigerian immunization schedule, which vaccine is given to a newborn baby right at birth?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid booster
options.B: Yellow fever vaccine
options.C: Measles vaccine
options.D: BCG vaccine

explanation: Correct! BCG protects babies against tuberculosis and is given right away at birth alongside the polio drops.

question: Why does a ventilation-perfusion mismatch happen when someone has a severe lung infection?

options.A: Blocked air sacs still get blood flow, but can't get fresh air.
options.B: The throat swells up and stops breathing completely.
options.C: The heart pumps blood way too slowly for the lungs.
options.D: Mucus plugs in the windpipe block blood from reaching the heart.

explanation: Think of it as a mismatch: blood is flowing past the air sacs ready to pick up oxygen, but because they are full of fluid, there's no fresh air waiting for them.

question: Why can't we use heavy weights in skin traction?

options.A: Too much weight causes bones to fuse together too quickly
options.B: Heavier weights will snap the traction rope instantly
options.C: Heavy weights interfere with the hospital overhead pulley system
options.D: Higher weights cause skin breakdown and tissue injury

explanation: Since the pull relies on soft tissues, too much weight will tear or blister the skin instead of helping the bone. Great job learning the basics!

question: A lab report describes tissue with disordered growth and cells of varying shapes and sizes. Which term describes this?

options.A: Metaplasia
options.B: Dysplasia
options.C: Hyperplasia
options.D: Atrophy

explanation: Well done! Dysplasia means disordered growth where cells lose their normal shape and organization—often an early warning sign that nurses watch closely.

question: Why does quitting cigarette smoking benefit a person's sexual health?

options.A: It causes immediate weight loss and lowers blood pressure
options.B: It replaces the need for hormonal balance in older adults
options.C: It preserves delicate blood vessels and nerve endings needed for arousal
options.D: It immediately cures all forms of inherited genetic disorders

explanation: Smoking damages blood vessels and impairs circulation, so stopping smoking protects the vascular pathways required for sexual response. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h6)

question: How does a glucometer turn a drop of blood into a number on the screen?

options.A: By taking a photo of the blood drop
options.B: By sensing the skin temperature of the finger
options.C: By measuring the electrical current from a chemical reaction
options.D: By weighing the plastic strip

explanation: When blood hits the strip, a tiny electrical current is produced. The meter reads this current and turns it into the number you see!

question: What are the classic signs of a fungal nail infection (onychomycosis)?

options.A: Soft, concave, spoon-shaped surfaces
options.B: Complete absence of the nail plate
options.C: Bright blue and swollen nail beds
options.D: Thick, yellow, and brittle nail plates

explanation: Well done! Fungal infections usually make the nail look discolored (yellow or brown), very thick, and easy to crumble.

question: Which legal concept allows nurses and doctors to treat an unconscious emergency patient without explicit consent?

options.A: Res ipsa loquitur
options.B: Emergency privilege
options.C: Vicarious liability
options.D: Professional indemnity

explanation: Correct! Emergency privilege assumes a patient would want life-saving care when they are unable to speak for themselves.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse must do after discovering a medication error?

options.A: Call the hospital lawyer to explain what happened
options.B: Fill out the institutional incident report form right away
options.C: Assess the patient's vital signs and current physical condition
options.D: Hide the medication packaging so nobody notices the mistake

explanation: Patient well-being always comes first! Always check your patient's condition before worrying about paperwork.

question: Which nursing intervention provides a simple, non-pharmacological method to relieve primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Placing the client in an absolute flat supine position
options.C: Encouraging immediate high-impact interval training
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

explanation: Heat relaxes uterine smooth muscle and helps reduce the ischemic pain associated with menstrual cramps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the main difference between palliative care and hospice care?

options.A: Hospice care is delivered exclusively in large government hospitals
options.B: Palliative care is only for cancer patients, whereas hospice is for everyone
options.C: Hospice care requires stopping curative treatments, while palliative care does not
options.D: Palliative care focuses strictly on spiritual healing rather than physical pain

explanation: Think of palliative care as a companion to curative treatment at any stage, while hospice specifically steps in when curative treatments are stopped.

question: What common health problem can happen when cultural food taboos stop pregnant women from eating meat and eggs?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Excessive fetal birth weight
options.C: Rapid maternal weight gain
options.D: Severe iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Brilliant! When expecting mothers miss out on protein and iron-rich foods, their bodies struggle to make enough red blood cells, leading to anemia.

question: How does activated charcoal help treat someone who swallowed a poison?

options.A: It dilates blood vessels to speed up renal excretion
options.B: It coats the lungs to block toxic gas inhalation
options.C: It binds to toxins in the gut to prevent their absorption into the bloodstream
options.D: It neutralizes stomach acid to prevent chemical ulcers

explanation: Activated charcoal acts like a microscopic sponge, holding onto the toxins in the stomach and gut so they don't enter the bloodstream.

question: Why do uric acid crystals cause such sudden, sharp pain in a joint?

options.A: White blood cells attack the crystals and release powerful inflammatory chemicals
options.B: The crystals physically cut the main nerve endings inside the joint capsule
options.C: Blood flow to the joint completely stops due to vessel blockage
options.D: Cartilage cells multiply so fast they stretch the joint to its breaking point

explanation: Think of white blood cells rushing in like an emergency crew to clear out the crystals—their cleanup effort triggers a massive wave of swelling and pain!

question: What are the main jobs of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile and filtering toxins from the blood
options.B: Secreting hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor
options.C: Digesting proteins and absorbing simple sugars
options.D: Absorbing water and compacting indigestible waste

explanation: Well done! The large intestine mainly soaks up remaining water and turns leftover food into solid stool ready for elimination.

question: How should a normal optic disc appear during a fundus examination?

options.A: Sharp, well-defined borders with a creamy pink or yellowish color
options.B: An irregular white scar tissue mass blocking the blood vessels
options.C: Blurred, swollen edges with dark purple patches throughout
options.D: A completely black circle surrounded by bright green rings

explanation: A healthy optic disc has crisp, distinct margins and a distinct yellowish-pink or creamy color without swelling. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a polygenic human trait?

options.A: Tongue rolling
options.B: Blood type ABO
options.C: Height
options.D: Huntington disease

explanation: Height is controlled by many different genes interacting together, making it a polygenic trait. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do with a mechanical weighing scale before a patient steps on it?

options.A: Wipe the platform with hot cooking oil
options.B: Place a thick mat underneath it
options.C: Lock the height rod permanently
options.D: Calibrate and balance it to zero

explanation: Always check that the scale starts right at zero! This ensures your weight reading is accurate and not thrown off by a previous reading.

question: Which tocolytic drug is usually avoided past 32 weeks because it can affect the baby's heart circulation?

options.A: Indomethacin
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Terbutaline
options.D: Nifedipine

explanation: Indomethacin is a prostaglandin blocker, but we have to be careful using it late in pregnancy so it doesn't cause early closure of the baby's ductus arteriosus. Excellent pharmacological safety!

question: An order reads: 1,000 mL normal saline over 8 hours. Your tubing drop factor is 15 gtt/mL. What is the flow rate?

options.A: 63 gtt/min
options.B: 15 gtt/min
options.C: 31 gtt/min
options.D: 125 gtt/min

explanation: Math made simple! Multiply total volume (1000) by drop factor (15) to get 15,000 drops, then divide by total minutes (480 mins). That gives you roughly 31 drops per minute.

question: Why must a mother with mastitis keep removing milk from the infected breast?

options.A: Pumping removes the need to take prescribed antibiotics
options.B: Stopping milk removal cures the infection faster
options.C: Continued drainage prevents further milk stasis and reduces infection severity
options.D: It prevents the baby from getting any nutrition

explanation: Emptying the breast stops milk from sitting stagnant, which is what bacteria love. Keeping it flowing helps her heal faster!

question: A nurse manager wants to tackle staff safety needs on a busy ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Provide adequate security and proper personal protective equipment
options.B: Organize a team-building social retreat
options.C: Nominate senior nurses for a national leadership award
options.D: Encourage staff to pursue advanced academic degrees

explanation: Spot on! Safety means being physically protected and having the right PPE before we worry about social activities or awards.

question: In the epidemiological triad, what do we call the actual germ or organism that causes a disease?

options.A: The infectious agent
options.B: The physical environment
options.C: The vector reservoir
options.D: The susceptible host

explanation: Spot on! The agent is the specific microorganism, like a bacterium or virus, that starts the infection in the triad model. You've got this!

question: A patient with a medullary stroke has a weak gag reflex and trouble swallowing. What is the most important nursing priority?

options.A: Checking passive range of motion in the limbs
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the neck muscles
options.C: Preventing food or liquid from entering the airway
options.D: Encouraging high fluid intake by mouth immediately

explanation: Impaired swallowing and a weak gag reflex lead straight to aspiration and pneumonia, making airway safety the primary concern. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)

question: A client suddenly shows a change in pupil size and a dropping GCS score. What does this most likely indicate?

options.A: Normal recovery from head trauma
options.B: An allergic reaction to hospital food
options.C: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.D: Rising pressure inside the skull

explanation: Unequal pupils and a worsening level of consciousness are classic warning signs that intracranial pressure is increasing dangerously. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T21#GNS222_U3_T21_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of non-pain symptom management in palliative care?

options.A: Speeding up the natural dying process safely
options.B: Curing the underlying terminal disease process
options.C: Eliminating the need for any medications
options.D: Maximizing patient comfort and quality of life

explanation: Palliative care focuses on comfort and quality of life when a cure is no longer possible. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h1)

question: Which complication of long bone fractures (like the femur) involves breathing trouble and a spotty rash?

options.A: Fat embolism syndrome
options.B: Osteomyelitis infection
options.C: Superficial skin breakdown
options.D: Chronic bone spur formation

explanation: Fat droplets from inside the bone marrow can slip into the bloodstream after a long bone break, traveling to the lungs and brain. Watch out for breathing issues and a petechial rash!

question: Why is psychological support also offered to the family members of a recovering patient?

options.A: To help them cope with stress and avoid caregiver burnout
options.B: To train them on how to perform physical therapy transfers
options.C: To evaluate their personal health insurance limits
options.D: To teach them how to administer prescription medications safely

explanation: Caring for a sick loved one is heavy work, both physically and emotionally. Supporting the family helps keep everyone healthy and strong!

question: A patient takes 15 seconds to complete the Timed Up and Go test. How should the nurse interpret this result?

options.A: The patient has normal mobility for an adult
options.B: The patient needs immediate cardiac monitoring
options.C: The patient has a high risk for falls
options.D: The patient requires upper limb strength training

explanation: A completion time exceeding 12 seconds on the TUG test is a standard indicator that an older adult is at an increased risk of falling. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h2)

question: Why do nurses always stress taking birth control pills at the exact same time every single day?

options.A: It ensures the monthly period starts on a weekend
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of the medication pack
options.C: It maintains steady hormone levels in the bloodstream
options.D: It prevents the client from forgetting to eat meals

explanation: Consistency is key! Taking it at the same time keeps hormone levels steady so breakthrough ovulation doesn't sneak through.

question: What actually happens when a man has a 'penile fracture'?

options.A: A severe calcium deficiency inside the bone structure of the pelvis
options.B: A tear in the protective outer sheath surrounding the erectile tissue
options.C: The complete detachment of the penis from the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: A clean break of the pubic bone underlying the base of the penis

question: What is one primary purpose of giving a shift report?

options.A: Providing a detailed history of the nurse's personal life
options.B: Eliminating the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Reducing the total number of working hours for hospital staff
options.D: Ensuring continuity of care across different nursing shifts

explanation: The shift report acts like a bridge between shifts, keeping patient care smooth and uninterrupted.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when planning an IEC activity?

options.A: Printing out colorful posters and flyers
options.B: Choosing which radio station will broadcast
options.C: Evaluating the final budget and expenses
options.D: Situation analysis and community assessment

explanation: Before jumping into action, a great nurse always checks the ground realities. You need to understand the community's actual needs and culture first!

question: What is the main goal of deep brain stimulation (DBS) for Parkinson's disease?

options.A: To surgically remove Lewy bodies from the cerebral cortex
options.B: To deliver electrical impulses that block abnormal brain signals
options.C: To regenerate lost dopamine-producing neurons in the midbrain
options.D: To replace damaged cerebrospinal fluid with synthetic dopamine

explanation: DBS uses tiny implanted wires to send gentle electrical pulses, acting like a pacemaker for the brain to block the faulty signals causing tremors and stiffness.

question: Why do doctors often add co-analgesics to a patient's treatment plan?

options.A: To cause immediate unconsciousness during surgical procedures
options.B: To speed up the physical healing of broken bones and fractures
options.C: To replace all nursing physical assessments of comfort levels
options.D: To target specific pain types and reduce opioid requirements

explanation: By teaming up different types of pain meds, we can tackle stubborn pain better and use lower, safer doses of heavy opioids.

question: Why can a needle look perfectly clean yet still carry a dangerous virus?

options.A: Microscopic traces of infected blood remain inside the hollow bore
options.B: Skin bacteria react with the metal to create new pathogens
options.C: The virus travels through the air surrounding the needle
options.D: Plastic needles absorb viruses and release them later

explanation: Even if you can't see it, an invisible film of fluid inside a needle hub holds enough viral particles to cause a new infection. That's why we never reuse needles!

question: What is looked at first when choosing drugs for the Nigerian Essential Medicines List?

options.A: How colorful the packaging of the drug is
options.B: The distance of the manufacturing country
options.C: Whether the drug has a pleasant sweet taste
options.D: Prevalence of the disease the drug treats

explanation: It's all about need! We prioritize drugs for the illnesses affecting the highest number of people in our communities.

question: Which part of the nervous system tells the bladder to contract so you can pee?

options.A: Sympathetic nervous system
options.B: Enteric nervous system
options.C: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.D: Somatic central nervous system

explanation: You got it! The parasympathetic system handles the 'rest and digest' activities—which includes telling the detrusor muscle it's time to empty the bladder.

question: What is the most common cause of blunt upper airway trauma in adults?

options.A: Sudden throat infections
options.B: Spontaneous tissue tears
options.C: Motor vehicle collisions
options.D: Severe allergic reactions

explanation: Spot on! Direct impacts from steering wheels or dashboards during car crashes frequently compress neck structures against the spine.

question: What is the most common side effect patients experience after a barium meal test?

options.A: Severe hair loss
options.B: Kidney failure
options.C: Internal bleeding
options.D: Constipation

explanation: You've got this! Because barium dries things out inside the bowel, constipation is the number one thing to watch out for afterward. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h7)

question: Why must a delivery kit with a torn or punctured wrapper be discarded or replaced?

options.A: The items inside will be too cold
options.B: The plastic becomes toxic over time
options.C: The manufacturer voids the warranty
options.D: The sterile barrier is broken

explanation: Any tear or hole allows air and environmental contaminants to enter, rendering the contents unsterile and unsafe for use. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h3)

question: How do the ovaries communicate back to the brain about their hormone levels?

options.A: By altering the physical size of the pituitary gland
options.B: By sending electrical impulses down the spinal cord
options.C: By sending estrogen and progesterone through the blood
options.D: By releasing white blood cells into lymphatic channels

explanation: Ovarian hormones travel through the bloodstream to send feedback signals back to the brain (the hypothalamus and pituitary gland). Simple and amazing how the body works!

question: Why do some topical medications bypass first-pass liver metabolism?

options.A: They are formulated to only stay in the top layer of skin cells
options.B: They enter the body without travelling through the digestive tract first
options.C: They require liver enzymes to activate their chemical structure
options.D: They are completely destroyed by skin enzymes before absorption

explanation: Because topical drugs are absorbed through the skin or mucous membranes rather than swallowed, they avoid the portal vein system that leads to early liver metabolism. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses love using local drama groups or folk songs during health campaigns?

options.A: They replace the need for professional medical advice
options.B: They prevent community members from asking questions
options.C: They are much cheaper than buying radio airtime
options.D: They utilize familiar cultural expressions to engage villagers

explanation: Using local art and language makes health messages feel welcoming, fun, and easy for the community to accept and understand.

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration
options.B: Normal kidney function for pregnancy
options.C: Potential underlying renal impairment
options.D: A normal non-pregnant baseline

explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now.

question: What two types of light do the LEDs inside a pulse oximeter probe emit?

options.A: Ultraviolet and green light
options.B: X-ray and fluorescent light
options.C: Blue and yellow laser light
options.D: Red and infrared light

explanation: The sensor relies on two specific light wavelengths, red and infrared, to differentiate between oxygenated and deoxygenated blood. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient walks into your clinic with constant headaches, tummy pain, and worry, but tests show nothing physically wrong. What should you keep in mind?

options.A: A congenital neurological disorder
options.B: A rare tropical infectious disease
options.C: Underlying trauma or domestic abuse
options.D: Acute food poisoning from expired food

explanation: When physical wounds heal or aren't there, survivors often show stress through ongoing body pains and anxiety. Always look a bit deeper!

question: What is a common myth among young people regarding Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?

options.A: Regular screening helps catch hidden diseases
options.B: Condoms can help prevent transmission
options.C: People with STIs always look visibly sick
options.D: Some infections do not show early symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Many people are surprised to learn that numerous STIs show no early symptoms at all, meaning someone can feel completely healthy while carrying an infection.

question: What is the first and most effective step to control external bleeding from a limb wound?

options.A: Applying a loose gauze wrap for comfort
options.B: Massaging the muscles above the injury
options.C: Pouring cold water over the injured area
options.D: Applying direct pressure to the wound

explanation: Direct pressure compresses the torn blood vessels, allowing the body's clotting factors to form a plug and stop the flow. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why is an IUD called a long-acting reversible contraceptive?

options.A: It only prevents pregnancy for a maximum of three months
options.B: It is permanent and cannot be taken out once inserted
options.C: It requires taking daily pills to stay effective
options.D: It protects against pregnancy for years, but fertility returns after removal

explanation: You get years of steady protection, but if the client ever wants to get pregnant later, you just take it out and her natural fertility bounces right back!

question: How should a nurse manager figure out how many safety boxes to order for next month?

options.A: By doubling the number of expired items thrown away last year
options.B: By matching the exact number of doctors on duty
options.C: Based on past patient use and expected service volume
options.D: By guessing a random number that fits on the form

explanation: Spot on! Smart ordering looks at past consumption trends and expected patient numbers so you don't overstock or run short.

question: Why do nurses use isolation techniques in the ward?

options.A: To speed up the patient's physical recovery
options.B: To prevent the spread of harmful microorganisms
options.C: To completely cure the underlying disease
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital medications

explanation: Isolation acts like a shield to stop germs from jumping between patients, staff, and visitors. Great job keeping the ward safe!

question: What do we call the tiny finger-like bits of the placenta that dip into the mother's blood to swap nutrients?

options.A: Umbilical rings
options.B: Amniotic folds
options.C: Chorionic villi
options.D: Decidua basalis

explanation: Great job! Chorionic villi are those lovely little finger-like projections that increase the surface area so the baby and mother can easily exchange nutrients and gases.

question: What is the primary role of a nurse acting as a patient advocate?

options.A: Refusing to talk with doctors about care plans
options.B: Suing the hospital administration whenever there is a treatment delay
options.C: Protecting the patient's rights, safety, and dignity when they cannot speak for themselves
options.D: Making all final medical decisions on behalf of the family

explanation: Brilliant! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients and keeping their best interests at heart.

question: Which nursing device is used to keep a patient's hips from rolling outward during bed rest?

options.A: Trochanter roll
options.B: Cervical neck collar
options.C: Overbed dining table
options.D: Hand roll pillow

explanation: A trochanter roll tucked snugly beside the thigh keeps the hip joint nice and neutral, stopping the leg from rolling outward.

question: How do most medicines actually produce their effects in our body?

options.A: By altering existing physiological processes
options.B: By changing the genetic code of human cells
options.C: By completely replacing natural body hormones
options.D: By creating entirely new cellular functions

explanation: Drugs don't usually invent brand new jobs for cells. Instead, they speed up or slow down things your body is already doing naturally!

question: Why is insulin considered the preferred medication for managing diabetes during pregnancy?

options.A: It does not cross the placenta in significant amounts
options.B: It stimulates the placenta to produce less growth hormone
options.C: It cures the underlying pancreatic beta-cell defect permanently
options.D: It can be taken orally instead of through painful injections

explanation: Insulin is a large protein molecule that does not readily cross the placental barrier, making it safe for the developing fetus while lowering maternal blood sugar. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h5)

question: How does hematogenous osteomyelitis differ from contiguous osteomyelitis?

options.A: Hematogenous only affects the skull, while contiguous affects long bones exclusively
options.B: Hematogenous is caused by viruses, whereas contiguous is always caused by fungi
options.C: Hematogenous spreads through the bloodstream, while contiguous comes from a nearby open wound or infection
options.D: Hematogenous occurs only in older adults, while contiguous is strictly pediatric

explanation: Think of 'hematogenous' as hitching a ride through the blood from somewhere else in the body, while 'contiguous' means the infection touched the bone directly from an outside wound nearby.

question: Under Nigerian law, when is an abortion legally allowed?

options.A: Whenever requested by the male partner or husband
options.B: Only when necessary to save the life of the pregnant woman
options.C: In all cases involving financial hardship or unemployment
options.D: Whenever the woman decides she is not ready for a child

explanation: Spot on. Nigerian law is quite strict and generally permits termination only if the mother's life is in direct danger.

question: Where in the body would you look for multi-unit smooth muscle?

options.A: In the walls of the urinary bladder
options.B: In the iris of the eye controlling the pupil
options.C: In the muscular walls of the stomach
options.D: In the middle layer of the small intestine

explanation: Multi-unit muscle gives us fine, precise control—just like adjusting your camera lens or how your iris changes the pupil size in bright light!

question: What do we call a loss that can be clearly seen and verified by everyone around, like losing a limb or a loved one?

options.A: A loss that is only felt internally by the affected individual
options.B: A loss of money or property caused by economic changes
options.C: A loss that occurs only during old age and natural retirement
options.D: A loss that can be recognized and verified by other people

explanation: Spot on! An actual loss is tangible. It's something both the patient and outsiders can clearly see, touch, or acknowledge, like an amputation or death.

question: Why is government funding for assistive devices like wheelchairs so important?

options.A: It makes devices like wheelchairs and hearing aids affordable for low-income citizens
options.B: It ensures that doctors receive higher salaries than other public workers
options.C: It prevents private hospitals from offering any medical services
options.D: It eliminates the need for physical therapy exercises at home

explanation: Good assistive tools can be very expensive. Government support helps bridge the financial gap so vulnerable patients aren't left behind.

question: How can a little bit of anxiety actually help someone during a tough moment?

options.A: It sharpens focus and prepares the body to face potential threats.
options.B: It completely eliminates any physical stress responses in the body.
options.C: It keeps the mind calm by preventing the release of stress hormones.
options.D: It guarantees that the person will avoid making any poor decisions.

explanation: Not all anxiety is bad! A healthy dose of adrenaline gives you that extra boost of alertness to face challenges—like writing a tough nursing OSCE.

question: Which patient symptom from an endemic region makes you suspect they might need a skin snip test?

options.A: Chronic intense itching and skin changes
options.B: Severe joint pain and high spiking fevers
options.C: Painful fluid-filled blisters on the lips
options.D: Sudden respiratory distress with wheezing

explanation: Spot on! Onchocerciasis (river blindness) is famous for causing stubborn, severe itching, bumps, and changes in skin texture where the parasite lives.

question: Why don't we pull back (aspirate) on the plunger anymore for routine subcutaneous shots like insulin?

options.A: It makes the medication completely inactive in the syringe
options.B: It increases the risk of the needle breaking in the skin
options.C: It causes unnecessary tissue trauma and increases bruising
options.D: It causes the plunger to stick permanently inside the barrel

explanation: Modern practice shows that the chance of hitting a vessel here is tiny. Pulling back just causes extra discomfort and bruising for no real benefit.

question: A patient is booked for an elective knee joint replacement. Which theatre is best suited for this?

options.A: Casualty theatre for minor trauma
options.B: Emergency trauma suite
options.C: Specialized orthopaedic theatre
options.D: General operating theatre

explanation: You got it! Joint surgeries need special tools and special airflow systems found in orthopaedic theatres to keep deep wounds free from infection.

question: Taking which class of medications for a long time is well-known to cause bone loss and muscle weakness?

options.A: Antihistamines
options.B: Antibiotics
options.C: Bronchodilators
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Correct! Long-term use of corticosteroids interferes with how the body handles calcium, often leading to bone thinning.

question: A team of student nurses investigates a sudden outbreak of measles in a single village. What kind of diagnosis are they doing?

options.A: Comprehensive community diagnosis
options.B: General environmental audit
options.C: Institutional demographic survey
options.D: Problem-oriented community diagnosis

explanation: Correct! Because they are zeroing in on one specific outbreak (measles), this is a classic problem-oriented approach.

question: Why might a nurse position an abdominal ultrasound patient to lie on their left side?

options.A: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.B: To shift bowel gas away from the organs being checked
options.C: To boost their blood pressure for the Doppler scan
options.D: To relax their tummy muscles completely

explanation: Shifting the patient's position helps move pesky gas-filled loops of the bowel out of the way of the ultrasound beam.

question: How does early substance abuse affect the brain's natural reward system?

options.A: It alters pathways so normal activities no longer bring pleasure
options.B: It stops the brain from producing any blood flow
options.C: It makes normal daily activities feel intensely rewarding
options.D: It permanently repairs damaged nerve cells in the brain

explanation: You got it! Drugs hijack natural reward pathways, draining dopamine levels so that everyday hobbies and joys suddenly feel dull.

question: Which nerve-related symptom is commonly linked to a vitamin B12 deficiency?

options.A: Sudden paralysis on one entire side of the body
options.B: Severe sharp pain radiating down the lower back
options.C: Inability to recognize familiar faces or places
options.D: Tingling and numbness in the hands and feet

explanation: Vitamin B12 is super important for nerve health. When you don't have enough, your peripheral nerves get irritated, causing that classic tingling and numbness (paresthesia).

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries?

options.A: Filtering waste and storing urine
options.B: Producing red blood cells and digesting fats
options.C: Producing gametes and secreting sex hormones
options.D: Manufacturing mucus and housing fetal tissue

explanation: The ovaries create egg cells and release hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient with diabetic foot neuropathy to test bathwater with their elbow instead of their feet?

options.A: Numbness in the feet prevents the patient from accurately sensing water temperature, risking scald burns
options.B: Elbow skin contains specialized sweat glands that neutralize toxic minerals found in tap water
options.C: Hot water causes immediate and permanent paralysis of the small motor nerves in the toes
options.D: The skin on the feet is biologically incapable of absorbing heat evenly compared to the upper body

explanation: Because neuropathy takes away normal feeling in the feet, patients might step into water that's way too hot without realizing it until they get burned. Using the elbow helps keep them safe!

question: What is the safest way to open the steam tent when the treatment is done?

options.A: Rip open the plastic tent quickly to let fresh air rush in
options.B: Leave the steam running while taking the patient out
options.C: Turn off the generator and open the canopy gradually
options.D: Wait until the room temperature drops below normal

explanation: Opening it slowly prevents a sudden blast of cool air from chilling your damp patient.

question: What is the primary objective of family planning counseling?

options.A: To eliminate population growth in developing nations completely
options.B: To force every woman of childbearing age to use hormonal contraception
options.C: To promote permanent surgical sterilization for all young couples
options.D: To help clients make informed choices about child spacing and family size

explanation: Family planning empowers clients with information to choose their preferred method safely and voluntarily. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is a complete blood count (CBC) useful when checking a patient with an unknown fever?

options.A: It measures exact prostaglandin levels in the blood
options.B: It shows the exact brain set point
options.C: It helps tell bacterial and viral infections apart using white blood cells
options.D: It tells you which mosquito species bit the patient

explanation: You're doing great! High white blood cells usually point to bacteria, helping us choose the right care.

question: What toxin buildup is primarily responsible for causing hepatic encephalopathy in liver failure?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Ammonia

question: Why is it important that the sexual partners of a patient treated for an STI-related infection also get treated?

options.A: To restore normal male hormones
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the patient and stop the spread
options.C: To prevent high blood pressure in partners
options.D: To make sure the partner doesn't get a tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: Treating partners breaks the chain of transmission. Otherwise, the patient could easily catch the infection all over again!
